equity_bridge.item: PLS Project (100%, Triple R deposit, Athabasca Basin) - 65% of disclosed post-tax NPV8 at this model's price deck
equity_bridge.note: SOURCED, not estimated. Paladin ASX announcement 'Patterson Lake South Project Update' and its presentation, 28 August 2025 (Engineering Review by Tetra Tech, building on Fission's 'Feasibility Study, NI 43-101 Technical Report, for PLS Property', effective 17 January 2023); figures restated unchanged in the 12 November 2026 equity-raising presentation. Disclosed: LOM production 90.9Mlb, 9.1Mlb/yr, 10-year initial mine life, 3-year construction, grade 1.41%, recovery 97%, cash operating cost US$11.7/lb, AISC US$15.2/lb, pre-production capital US$1,226M (C$1,635M) incl. US$109M contingency, LOM sustaining capital US$325M incl. contingency, closure US$74M, first production targeted 2031; post-tax (27% corporate rate) NPV at 8% REAL from start of construction: US$472M at $60/lb, 617 at $65, 759 at $70, 1,043 at $80, 1,325 at $90 (IRR 28.2%, payback 2.4 years), 1,609 at $100, 1,891 at $110, 2,172 at $120; average FCF US$379M/yr at $80. Cross-check that royalties are inside 'post-tax': at $80 the disclosed FCF is ~US$41.6/lb against a pre-tax margin of ~US$64.7/lb after cash cost and sustaining capital, a ~US$23/lb take versus ~US$15/lb for 27% tax alone, so ~10% of revenue in Saskatchewan royalties is already deducted. HOW IT IS USED: 8% real is this model's 10% nominal WACC less the 2% escalation in its price deck, so the company's NPV8 is taken at face rather than rebuilt. Base deck US$80/lb in FY2029 money = ~US$74/lb in the study's mid-2025 money -> NPV8 ~US$873M (interpolated) -> x1.03 to late-2026 dollars, / 1.08^1.6 for the ~1.6 years to a mid-2028 construction start = ~US$795M unrisked today -> x 65% = ~US$517M. Bull deck (~US$89 real) ~US$1,180M unrisked x 80% = ~945; bear deck (~US$55 real, below the table's lowest row, extrapolated) ~US$270M x 30% = ~80. Weighted 25/50/25 = US$515M. The 65% risking is carried over unchanged from the first build and covers: no FID yet; CNSC Construction Licence hearings only targeted (non-binding) for end CY2027; the Metis Nation-Saskatchewan judicial review of the February 2026 provincial EIS approval; capex escalation (the 2023 FS figure rose ~40% in the 2025 review and this is still a FEED-stage estimate in mid-2025 dollars); and the unarranged funding package for US$1,226M. No value is taken for the 118.8Mlb Indicated / 10.9Mlb Inferred resource beyond the 90.9Mlb mine plan, nor for the Atlas and Saloon East discoveries. Book value of exploration and evaluation is US$538M.

equity_bridge.item: PLS pre-FID capital works programme CY2027-28 (funded from the November 2026 raising)
equity_bridge.note: US$252M (A$367M) 'PLS Project development spend CY2027 and CY2028' in the uses of funds of the A$525M raising (12 November 2026 presentation, 'Sources and uses'): EPCM/owner's costs 51, site infrastructure and enabling works 75, processing plant long-lead items 81, underground mine development 45. The same presentation footnotes the US$1,226M pre-production capital as 'exclusive of pre-FID capital expenditure', so this spend is treated as additional to the capital inside the disclosed NPV and deducted in full (it is spent whether or not the project is sanctioned), discounted ~1.2 years at 10%. CONSERVATIVE AND AMBIGUOUS: long-lead plant and underground development would normally be part of pre-production capital; if this programme is in fact inside the US$1,226M, this deduction double-counts and should be removed (worth ~US$0.43 / ~A$0.64 per share). No Canadian tax shield is credited. The further US$70M earmarked for Triple R resource growth and Athabasca exploration is discretionary and not deducted.

equity_bridge.item: Michelin Project (Labrador, 100%) and Australian projects - nominal resource value, no economic study
equity_bridge.note: NOT an NPV. Michelin is described by Paladin as an 'advanced exploration project' (FY2026 Annual Report; H1 FY2026 report), held through Aurora Energy Ltd (acquired February 2011 per the FY2016 Annual Report; interest rose from 75% to 100% on 18 October 2023 when the JV partners diluted out). Resources at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR Table 3, partly JORC 2004): Measured 38.0Mlb, Indicated 67.6Mlb, Inferred 22.1Mlb = 127.7Mlb at ~0.06-0.10% U3O8. Paladin discloses no PEA, PFS or FS for Michelin, no capex, no operating cost and no schedule; FY2026 activity was US$6.6M of exploration and a ~54% tenure reduction. Carried at US$50M for Michelin plus the Australian projects (Queensland bans uranium mining; Western Australia has a no-development policy) = under US$0.50/lb of Michelin Measured and Indicated resource - a deliberately low in-ground multiple for long-dated, unpermitted, low-grade pounds. Unchanged from the first build.

scenario_narratives.base: Langer Heinrich delivers the middle of FY2027 guidance (about 5.05Mlb sold) with costs at the top of the US$44-48/lb range after a US$61.6/lb first quarter, then reaches ~5.9Mlb/yr of sales by FY2029 and holds it while in-situ reserves last (to ~FY2034), stepping down to ~5Mlb as the plant blends low-grade stockpiles with converted resources. Realised price, already ~US$79/lb in Q1 FY2027 against spot near US$90, is held at a US$80/lb mid-cycle level in FY2029 and then tracks inflation; the current term market is treated as above mid-cycle. Cost of production falls to ~US$41/lb on fixed-cost dilution and J Pit grade. The mine earns ~37% EBITDA margins, but Paladin shareholders keep only about a third of EBIT once Namibian tax resumes (losses exhausted ~FY2030) and CNNC takes its 25%. PLS is carried at 65% of the post-tax NPV8 the company disclosed in its August 2025 Engineering Review, read at this price deck, less the CY2027-28 pre-FID works the November 2026 raising pays for.
scenario_narratives.bull: The supply deficit the industry forecasts for the 2030s arrives: term contracts reprice toward US$100/lb by FY2031 and Paladin's market-related volumes capture it. The plant runs at 6Mlb nameplate, resource definition drilling on ML140 converts enough of the 86Mlb Measured and Indicated in-situ resource to keep full-grade feed through FY2036, and unit costs settle at ~US$39-40/lb. Margins reach ~48%. PLS would be worth roughly US$945M risked in this world (disclosed NPV8 of ~US$1.3bn at ~US$90/lb real), against the US$515M in the single bridge.
scenario_narratives.bear: Uranium repeats its history: utilities defer contracting, secondary supply and Kazakh/Cameco restarts fill the gap, and realised price slides to ~US$60/lb as market-related contracts reset and floors bind. The Q1 FY2027 recovery problems (85% versus 90%) prove persistent: LHM plateaus at 5.5Mlb with cost of production stuck at ~US$44/lb, leaving the mine roughly break-even after capitalised stripping, stockpiling and G&A; free cash flow is slightly negative for FY2029-FY2034 and only turns positive in the low-cost stockpile phase. No mine-life extension. PLS still shows a positive disclosed NPV8 at US$60/lb (US$472M, IRR 16.4%), but at this deck (~US$55/lb in the study's money) and after any capex overrun sanction is doubtful; it would be worth ~US$80M as an option against the US$515M in the bridge, so the bridge overstates it here. The 2018 precedent is that the company puts the mine back on care and maintenance rather than run at a loss.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Paladin is valued as a finite-life mine plus a development project, not as a growing cash-flow stream. Langer Heinrich's cash flows are built from volume, realised contract price and unit cost over the reserve life, with no perpetuity; the share that reaches Paladin holders is cut by Namibian tax, CNNC's 25% and corporate overhead. PLS is added at 65% of the post-tax NPV8 from the company's own feasibility-level study, read at a US$80/lb (FY2029 money) deck rather than the study's US$90, less the pre-FID spend. On that price and a 10% discount rate the equity is worth well under the market price: the market is paying for a uranium price near or above US$100/lb sustained, and/or PLS at close to unrisked value.
key_risks_to_valuation: Uranium price is the dominant driver: each US$10/lb on realised price is worth roughly US$0.35-0.40/share (about A$0.55) on Langer Heinrich alone, and more through PLS.

PLS (net of pre-FID spend) is about a quarter of base equity value and pro forma net cash about half. The PLS figures are now the company's disclosed Engineering Review numbers, but they are a FEED-stage estimate in mid-2025 dollars: capex already rose ~40% on the 2023 Feasibility Study. The 65% risking and the reading of the pre-FID programme as additional to the US$1,226M are my judgements; treating the programme as inside the US$1,226M adds ~A$0.64/share.

Cash and share count are pro forma for a placement that settles on 18 November 2026, three days after the valuation date; the non-underwritten SPP is excluded. FY2027 guidance ranges come from the Analysis JSON, confirmed as unchanged by the September-quarter report.
The combined tax/CNNC leakage rate is a calibration at steady-state EBIT; it is less accurate when EBIT is far from that level, and Priority Loan repayments (which favour Paladin) are not modelled.
Mine life: reserves support ~8 years at nameplate plus stockpiles; value beyond FY2036 depends on resource conversion and is represented only by the terminal cap multiple.
Namibian fiscal and regulatory change (royalty, export levy, local-ownership rules) and the shareholder class action (unquantified) are not in the numbers.

Sell-side targets of A$9.70-15.80 sit far above this value. Using a US$100/lb deck and PLS at ~US$945M (the bull inputs) still gives well under the market price at a 10% discount rate; unrisked PLS at the study's own US$90/lb (US$1,325M) would add roughly A$1.50/share to the base.

inputs.share_count_basis: PRO FORMA for the A$525M equity raising completed 13 November 2026: 449.358M ordinary shares on issue (30 June 2026, unchanged at 30 September per the raising presentation's 449.4M) + ~64.0M ASX placement shares at A$7.80 + ~3.3M TSX bought-deal shares at C$7.62 (67.3M new shares; settlement 18 November, allotment 19 November 2026; fully underwritten, bookbuild complete) + 2.019M performance rights + ~0.16M shares from exercised-but-unconverted share appreciation rights = 518.8M. The non-underwritten SPP (up to A$50M, ~6.4M shares at A$7.80, booklet due ~23 November) is EXCLUDED: it is not committed and is priced above the market price at inputs.price_as_of. Held flat thereafter because SBC is expensed in the flows. The raising covers PLS spend only to FID; the US$1,226M pre-production capital still needs a funding package (debt process is early-stage, indicative terms non-binding), and that remaining dilution/financing risk is carried in the 65% risking of the PLS bridge value, not in the share count.
inputs.net_debt_note: PRO FORMA. Cash and investments US$209M at 30 September 2026 (Quarterly Report - September 2026, 14 Oct 2026) + net raising proceeds US$345M (A$525M gross less A$16M offer costs = A$509M, converted at this model's 0.6774; the company's own pro forma uses 0.6878 and shows US$570M cash gross of costs) = US$554M. Debt = Term Loan US$28M at 30 September (to be repaid from proceeds; net-cash neutral) + lease liabilities US$6.5M (30 June 2026, latest disclosed). EXCLUDES the US$116.8M CNOL (CNNC) shareholder loans to LHU: those are CNNC's 25% funding interest in Langer Heinrich and are charged once, through the 25% leakage inside the cash_tax_rate_path. Roughly US$252M of this cash is committed to the PLS CY2027-28 pre-FID works programme, which is deducted separately in equity_bridge. Small overlap, conservative: cash is struck at 30 September while the FY2027 flow still contains the September quarter, in which cash fell US$56M.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF 37.726 less PP&E 16.649, exploration & evaluation 32.435 and capitalised stripping 16.766 (FY2026 cash flow statement). OCF is already after US$35.0M of low-grade ore stockpiling capitalised to non-current inventory.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report statement of changes in equity, share-based payments US$4,076k (line 9930); no net-share-settlement tax line in financing activities
inputs.fx_note: USD->AUD 1.4762 = 1/0.6774 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-11-14T10:27Z). Parity check against the TSX listing: PDN.TO C$6.91 x 0.7008 (CADUSD=X) = US$4.84 versus PDN.AX A$7.17 x 0.6774 = US$4.86, a 0.3% tie that confirms rate, direction and quote basis.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.0% nominal USD, built in the flows' currency: ~4.3% US 10-year risk-free + ~5% equity risk premium x beta ~1.15 for the unlevered asset; net cash so no debt weighting. Same WACC in all three scenarios. Uranium-price, single-asset and Namibian fiscal risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in a WACC premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt): US$6.5M lease liabilities included in total_debt, principal not deducted from the flows. Immaterial either way (US$1.7M/yr principal).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Langer Heinrich is 75% Paladin / 25% CNNC (CNOL). The cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED leakage rate on group EBIT: Namibian cash tax (37.5% mining rate, sheltered by US$458M of unrecognised Namibian tax losses for roughly the first three to four years) + CNNC's 25% share of LHM after-tax free cash flow + the fact that ~US$34M/yr of corporate G&A sits inside group EBIT but shields neither Namibian tax nor CNNC's share. Calibrated at steady state: ~30% while losses shelter tax, ~67% once full tax applies (base); 28% / 61% in bull (larger EBIT dilutes the G&A effect). The CNOL shareholder loans and the NCI equity balance are therefore NOT deducted again in the bridge. Conservative on one point: Priority Loans from Paladin to LHU rank ahead of the shareholder loans, so early LHM cash goes to Paladin at more than 75%; the size of the Priority Loans is eliminated on consolidation and not disclosed in the folder's filings, so no credit is taken.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route) with the cyclical/non-US adaptations, built as a mine-life volume x price model rather than an extrapolation of the ramp-up. Routing: an operating company (single producing mine) -> owner-FCF + adaptations; no mining-specific row exists in the routing table, so the commodity adaptations are applied inside the driver paths. (1) REVENUE = sales volume (Mlb U3O8) x realised price (US$/lb), not a growth rate off history. FY2016-FY2025 are not representative: LHM was in care and maintenance FY2019-FY2024 and FY2025 was a part-year ramp; only FY2026 (4.82Mlb produced, 4.35Mlb sold, US$70.0/lb realised, cost of production US$43.3/lb) informs unit economics, and it is still below the ~6Mlb nameplate. (2) PRICE: revenue uses contract-book realised price, not spot. FY2026 realised US$70/lb sat ~20% below spot (UX futures ~US$90/lb, last Yahoo print 2026-10-22) because of legacy fixed-price and base-escalated contracts; 21Mlb is contracted to 2030. Base mid-cycle is US$80/lb in FY2029 money (roughly the incentive price for new supply), reached as legacy contracts roll off, then +2%/yr with costs escalating in parallel. (3) FINITE LIFE: LHM Ore Reserves at 30 June 2026 are 70.4Mlb contained (52.7Mlb in-situ at ~480ppm, 17.7Mlb stockpiles at 326ppm) = roughly 8 years of in-situ feed at nameplate then a lower-grade stockpile phase. The terminal value is therefore NOT a perpetuity: terminal growth is 0 and the cap multiple (4x base, 2x bear, 6x bull) binds, standing for the remaining stockpile/resource-conversion years after FY2036. The sensitivity grid is consequently flat across terminal growth. (4) CAPEX path includes sustaining PP&E, capitalised stripping, low-grade ore stockpiling (US$35M in FY2026, booked in operating cash flow by the company) and ~US$8M/yr of exploration; PLS development spend is excluded from the flows and sits in the PLS bridge value. (5) PLS and Michelin sit in equity_bridge, now on SOURCED figures (see data_sources.pls_project / michelin_project and the bridge notes). PLS (Patterson Lake South, Saskatchewan, 100%, acquired with Fission Uranium Corp. in December 2024) has a completed Feasibility Study (NI 43-101, effective 17 January 2023) and a FEED-stage cost update (Paladin 'PLS Project Update', 28 August 2025): 90.9Mlb over a 10-year life, 9.1Mlb/yr, cash cost US$11.7/lb, AISC US$15.2/lb, pre-production capital US$1,226M, LOM sustaining capital US$325M, closure US$74M, 3-year construction, first production 2031; post-tax NPV8 (real) US$1,043M at US$80/lb and US$1,325M at US$90/lb. It is valued as a risked share of that disclosed NPV, read off the company's own price-sensitivity table at this model's price deck. Michelin (Labrador, 100% via Aurora Energy Ltd, acquired February 2011; went from 75% to 100% in October 2023) is an advanced EXPLORATION project with a resource and NO current economic study, so it is carried at a nominal resource value, not an NPV. One bridge serves all scenarios (the engine carries one), so per-scenario values understate the bull-bear spread: risked PLS would be ~US$945M in bull and ~US$80M in bear against the US$515M carried; the weighted IV is approximately right. (6) Inventory: 1.69Mlb finished product less 0.40Mlb owed under uranium product loans = 1.29Mlb, treated as normal pipeline, no bridge item. (7) Interest income stripped (net cash material). (8) No buybacks, no dividends; flat count is a modelling convention. VINTAGE: cash and term loan are at 30 September 2026 and both cash and share count are pro forma for the A$525M placement announced 12 November and completed 13 November 2026 (settlement 18 November); the price at inputs.price_as_of is the first close after the raising, so price and share count are on the same basis. The September-quarter report (1.00Mlb produced, 1.16Mlb sold, realised US$79.4/lb, cost of production US$61.6/lb, FY2027 guidance reaffirmed) was read from the company's website on 2026-11-15; it is not in the Extracted folder. FY2027 guidance ranges (production 5.1-5.6Mlb, sales 4.8-5.3Mlb, cost US$44-48/lb, LHM capex US$29-35M) are from PDN.AX_Analysis.json; the quarterly confirms the production range and that guidance is unchanged. LHM driver paths are UNCHANGED from the first build. The price is near the bottom of its 52-week range (6.82-15.10) after roughly halving from the high; the weak September quarter and the discounted placement (A$7.80 against a prior close of A$8.70) are the visible causes. Sell-side targets cited in the Analysis JSON (A$9.70-15.80) are three to five times this model's value: the gap is the uranium price deck, the discount rate and near-unrisked PLS value, and it is the main thing a reader should weigh.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 4x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to a symmetric 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: a single operating asset in a commodity that spent 2011-2021 below the cost of production, which already put this mine on care and maintenance once. Base 50%: mid-cycle price at the incentive level with FY2026 unit costs improving modestly at nameplate. Bull cut to 25%: it needs a sustained US$100/lb term market, nameplate throughput and resource conversion together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
